title: GIC & Temasek Sovereign Wealth Side Letter — Sovereign Immunity & MFN Tier Redlines
initialRequestBrief: Meridian Global Infrastructure GP III is negotiating side letters with two sovereign wealth fund investors ahead of the 30 September 2025 first close: Sovereign Investor A (US$80M) and Sovereign Investor B (US$35M), both represented by Ashcombe Lim LLP. Investor counsel has signalled that neither can accept the standard investor indemnity in Subscription Agreement Section 6.2 or a submission to jurisdiction, and both want visibility of fee terms granted to other LPs under the MFN. The GP needs compromise language that protects the partnership without making status-based concessions electable by every LP, and an MFN compendium Ops can generate after the final close.
summary: Two sovereign wealth LPs rejected the standard investor indemnity on statutory-immunity grounds and demanded global MFN fee visibility. Four redline rounds over three weeks produced a pre-approved Sovereign Immunity Reservation Clause, a set-off-and-cap replacement for the indemnity, and MFN fee disclosure split into US$25M and US$50M+ brackets.
howItWent: Round 1 from investor counsel struck the indemnity and the submission to jurisdiction and asked to see every fee term granted to any LP; the GP rejected both. Round 2 from GP counsel waived the indemnity in an untagged clause, which would have let every LP above US$25M elect it through the MFN, so it was withdrawn. David Le drafted Round 3 from Anduin's clause library: an immunity reservation that keeps the commercial obligations binding and preserves remedies against the Interest, plus set-off capped at the value of the Interest, both tagged as Excluded Provisions. Investor counsel accepted that in principle, but Sovereign Investor B then asked to see the US$50M+ fee terms. Round 4 split MFN fee disclosure into commitment brackets with affiliate aggregation, and both counsel approved it on 12 September 2025, three weeks after kickoff.
resolutionSteps: Adopt the pre-approved Sovereign Immunity Reservation Clause: reserve all immunities while acknowledging that capital contributions, distribution clawbacks and set-off amounts remain binding commercial obligations, and preserve the GP's remedies against the Interest.
Replace the investor indemnity with a set-off right capped at the value of the investor's Interest and recovered only from that Interest.
Tag every status-based sovereign concession as an Excluded Provision so it is disclosed but never electable under the MFN.
Structure MFN fee disclosure into commitment brackets (US$25M-49.99M and US$50M+), aggregating commitments of vehicles controlled by the same state.
Generate the MFN compendium from the clause-by-clause eligibility matrix, and hard-fail when an LP has no recorded bracket.

pitfalls.warning: An untagged side-letter clause is an Electable Provision: waiving the indemnity for a sovereign in a plain clause lets every LP at the MFN threshold elect it.
pitfalls.author: david.le

pitfalls.warning: Don't negotiate the immunity itself. Reserve it, carve out the commercial obligations, and rely on remedies exercised inside the partnership, which need no court.
pitfalls.author: david.le

pitfalls.warning: Without affiliate aggregation a sovereign can split its commitment across two vehicles to pick its MFN bracket.
pitfalls.author: david.le

pitfalls.warning: The compendium generator must never default a missing bracket to US$25M; the administrator records each bracket first (Section 5(e)).
pitfalls.author: chloe.nguyen
